input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: The only licence grant to us is § 4(c) (p0021), covering Contractor's Information embedded in the Works. It meets the preferred position on the material terms: the licence is perpetual and royalty-free with no revocation right reserved to Contractor (nothing makes it revocable at Contractor's discretion or terminable other than for the express contract remedies), it is broad in scope ("in connection with Company's business operations", including modification and derivative works), and it includes an unrestricted right to grant sublicences, which gives us a path to extend use to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf without notice or consent — better than the fallback (affiliates on written notice). § 4(d) (p0022) reinforces this by letting us engage third parties to modify the software. Non-exclusivity is expected for a vendor's background IP and is not a concern. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal wording and are noted rather than flagged: the grant does not say "irrevocable" expressly, and successor transfer runs through the mutual assignment clause (p0042), which requires consent that "will not be unreasonably withheld" rather than a carve-out for M&A successors — that assignment mechanic is addressed under the assignment rule and is not double-flagged here. No walk-away features (no vendor-discretionary revocation, no exclusion of affiliates/contractors).
